# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — first capability: no-formula value contract + write-in-place + examples-as-spec + verify-then-stop
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md grading contract (cluster A: formulas read as None under no-recalc).
  - openpyxl write-in-place pattern + index→Excel-row rule (B).
  - Examples-in-range are the spec; fill every cell; inspect beyond the preview (C).
  - Verify printout, Excel semantics notes, color rgb[-6:] rule (D).
  - task_template.md: ordered inspect→solve→verify→finish procedure replacing "once that file exists, you are done" (E).
- Expected effect:
  - Fix most formula-writers: 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942, 55979, 53647, 54144, 37456, 9569, 56563.
  - Possibly 50768, 48527, 39046, 59196, 267-18, 43436.
  - Safe: passing tasks already write literal values. to_excel is discouraged, not forbidden.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- Not cracked / untargeted: 80-42 (big consolidation), 51-12 (odd logic), 227-40 (header + dedup).
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration:
  - Read the RESULT broke-list. If passing to_excel tasks broke, soften the Method section further.
  - If formula tasks still fail, check the traces for whether the agent obeyed.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.846 Δ=+0.396 · fixed={227-40, 267-18, 37378, 39046, 46897, 53383, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={—} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: diagnose failures by diffing init vs golden workbooks (data_only) against the agent's final code, rather than by the feedback text alone. It revealed that the scoring mode (hard_no_recalc) makes formula-writing a single dominant cluster (~1/3 of failures). Outcome: see RESULT.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next iteration:
  - If A-cluster tasks remain failing, inspect whether the agent still emitted "=" strings, i.e. the contract was ignored, versus it computing values wrongly.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001 (spreadsheetbench)
- A stray `/tmp/struct.py` in the environment shadows the stdlib `struct` module for any python run with cwd=/tmp, which breaks openpyxl/pandas imports during analysis. Clean /tmp or warn in INSTRUCTIONS.
- INSTRUCTIONS should state the reward mode (e.g. hard_no_recalc = no formula recalculation) prominently. It is the single most decisive fact for this benchmark, and I had to dig it out of the adapter/env.
- A small read-only helper that dumps init vs golden values for the answer range of a failing task would save most of the diagnosis time.

files.name: PROCESS.md
files.title: Process — best candidate (cand_0001)
files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration cand_0001: the first capability, written from scratch. Baseline: empty prompt.md, built-in template, val 0.450 (18/40).
Metric: hard_no_recalc. The grader loads the output with data_only=True and does no recalculation.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula written instead of a value | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942, 55979, 56563, 37456, 53647, 54144, 9569 (~13) | The agent writes "=..." with openpyxl, which has no cached value, so the grader reads None. The instruction often says "formula"/"VBA". | KNOWLEDGE (grading contract) | CONTRACT rule in prompt.md + restated in the template's solve step |
| 2 | B. Rebuilt via to_excel / row-index shift | 48527, 50768, 227-40, 80-42 | pandas index ≠ Excel row, so the header row is dropped and existing cells are overwritten | BEHAVIORAL (method) | METHOD: openpyxl write-in-place pattern + index→row mapping rule |
| 3 | C. Example cells ignored / range not fully filled | 39046, 59196, 54144, 227-40 | Pre-filled cells in the target range are the gold pattern, but the agent wrote a total / partial / None. Headers were on row 2. | KNOWLEDGE | "examples are the spec" + "fill every cell" + "inspect beyond the preview" |
| 4 | D. Wrong interpretation, not verified | 43436, 51-12, 267-18 | Wrong aggregation (per-row instead of per-category×month), wrong color match (red counted as yellow) | BEHAVIORAL | VERIFY step: re-open the output and print the answer range; matrix-aggregation note; rgb[-6:] color rule |
| 5 | E. Repetition loops until 30 turns | 227-40, 37456, 2768 (pass), others | "Code executed with no output", so the agent resubmits the same code. The built-in template says "once that file exists, you are done". | BEHAVIORAL (loop) | Template: ordered inspect→solve→verify→finish; reply without code to stop; never resend identical code |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CONTRACT | prompt.md "How your output is graded" + task_template step 2 | States why formulas score None. Always write computed literal values, even for formula/VBA asks. Recompute any source formula cell whose cached value is missing or an error. Applies to any task under no-recalc scoring. | Yes. All 18 passing traces already write values. |
| B | METHOD | prompt.md "Method" code pattern | Read with a data_only copy, write the target cells on the original workbook, save. Explicit mapping: DataFrame index i = Excel row i+2 (header) or i+1 (header=None). | Worded as "prefer", not "forbid". The 13 passing to_excel users keep a valid path. Blast radius MODERATE: the output-writing style changes. |
| C | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md "Understand" 1–4 | Existing values are examples to reproduce. Fill every cell. Per-row criteria. Header row when the range includes it. Headers may sit below row 1. | Yes. It only adds inspection/consistency checks. |
| D | BEHAVIORAL + KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md "Verify" + Understand 5–6 | Re-open the output with data_only and print the answer range. Excel semantics notes (EOMONTH, case-insensitive COUNTIF, blank → None). Colors compared on the last 6 hex digits. | Yes. |
| E | BEHAVIORAL | task_template.md tail | Replaces "once that file exists, you are done" with a 4-step procedure. Finish = plain-text reply (the adapter stops on no-code after a solution exists). Do not resend identical code. | Yes. It also cuts the 30-turn loops seen on passing 2768. |

## Verify-the-fix (the trace each change targets → what the capability now does on those inputs)
- A / 55979, 53647, 54144, 37456, 9569: each trace wrote `ws[c] = "=..."` and got None. The contract now requires Python-computed literals. I checked the golden values are plain numbers/strings (e.g. 8.75, 10; 37.46, 48.02), so literals match. 56563: the init source cell is '#NUM!'; the recompute-from-inputs rule covers it.
- B / 50768: `to_excel(header=None)` shifted the grid. The pattern writes by coordinate (H12, F14, G14), and the expected values '4, 6' / '1, 3, 5' / '2' are strings, which the format rule covers. 48527: write-in-place keeps D2/D3, which already match.
- C / 39046: F2:F6 init holds examples 2, 2, 0. The rule "computed values must reproduce the examples" rejects the grand-total answer. 59196: H3 = 'D' example, headers on row 2, handled by "headers may sit on row 2".
- D / 267-18: I verified the init fills: G1 = FF00B050 (green), G2 = FFFFFF00. The yellow = 'FFFF00' rule excludes G1. 43436: the note on one aggregated value per (row, column) plus EOMONTH date semantics targets the I2:K6 dept×month count.
- E: the template renders with all 7 placeholders. `adapter._task_template_error(cand)` returned None, and `_read_system_prompt` returned 5868 chars.

## Process & features used
- Serial fallback: the session instructions forbid the Agent tool / workflows unless the user requests them. The analysis used read-only python scripts in /tmp/me_cmp comparing init vs golden workbooks and the trajectories.
- Prior iterations: none (this is the first candidate). RUNMAP / rejected.jsonl hold no prior rejects.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The never-write-formulas contract (it decides pass/fail under hard_no_recalc).
- The verify printout + "reply without code to finish" (prevents 30-turn loops).
- Examples-in-range-are-the-spec.

## Deliberately skipped
- 80-42 (large multi-sheet consolidation, 8512 cells). This is a capability/complexity issue. The method edit may help, but it is not specifically targeted.
- 51-12 (obscure "increase marker" logic): only the generic examples/verify guidance applies. There is no task-specific hint, to avoid overfitting.
- A custom tool/helper file: the adapter exposes only prompt.md/task_template.md, so no tool lever is available.

---

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate

# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
or give a worked example it can pattern-match. Prose is for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a
fact / format / criterion the agent cannot derive) and for STRUCTURE that changes what the
agent does — not for repetition or emphasis.

## The THREE TESTS every change must pass (this is the whole game)
Before you keep any edit, confirm all three. Drop any edit that fails even one.
1. **REAL** — it targets a cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`

2. **SAFE (bounded blast radius)** — the real regression question is *behavioral*:

   - **UNBOUNDED** — any edit to a GLOBAL decision/permission/refusal rule, or a …[+13631 chars truncated]
